meta.date: The practice of the church, written out by Moroni after AD 400
meta.unit: Baptism, membership, and how the church met (Moroni 6)
principles: Names written down so people could be looked after

world_behind.title: The officers were baptized too
world_behind.text: Verse 1 lists elders, priests, and teachers among those who came to the water. 3 Nephi 19:11 and 12 has Nephi go down into the water and be baptized before he baptizes anyone else, so the order has a precedent in the visit itself.

world_behind.title: The entry requirements match the waters of Mormon
world_behind.text: Mosiah 18:8 to 10 has Alma requiring willingness to bear one another's burdens, to mourn with those that mourn, and to stand as witnesses of God, before baptism. Verses 1 through 3 here list fruit, a broken heart, a witness to the church, and a determination to serve to the end. The bar has been in use since the church was founded.

world_behind.title: Keeping names is one of the oldest practices in the book
world_behind.text: Mosiah 6:1 has king Benjamin take the names of everyone who entered the covenant, and Mosiah 26:35 has Alma number the repentant among the people of the church. Verse 4 records the practice still running four hundred years later, and gives the reason: that they might be remembered and nourished.

world_behind.title: Blotting out a name is also older than this chapter
world_behind.text: Mosiah 26:36 has those who would not confess and repent removed from the number of the church, with their names blotted out. Verse 7 keeps the same discipline and the same escape from it.

world_behind.title: Three witnesses is the standard of the law
world_behind.text: Deuteronomy 19:15 requires two or three witnesses to establish a matter. Verse 7 keeps the number in a church that 4 Nephi 1:12 says had stopped walking after the performances and ordinances of the law of Moses.

world_behind.title: Meeting often is reported, not commanded
world_behind.text: Verses 5 and 6 both use "oft," once for fasting and prayer and once for bread and wine. 4 Nephi 1:12 says the same of the generation after the visit. Moroni is describing a habit that outlasted three centuries.

world_behind.title: This is the last thing he records about how the church ran
world_behind.text: Verse 9 lists five things the Spirit might lead them to do and leaves the choice open. Moroni 7 turns from procedure to a sermon of his father's, and the practice chapters do not resume.

words.text: A settled resolve. The record uses the word five times and the King James Bible once. Verse 3 attaches it to serving him to the end.
What someone has earned, offered on another's behalf. Treated at 2 Nephi 31:19. Verse 4 says they relied alone upon them.
The one who brings a thing to completion. The word appears once in the record, here, and once in the King James Bible, at Hebrews 12:2.
Frequently. Treated at 1 Nephi 18:3. The record uses the word sixteen times and the King James Bible thirteen. Verses 5 and 6 use it twice in two lines.
Struck off a written record. Treated at Mosiah 5:11. It appears eight times in the record and six in the King James Bible.
Admitted openly. The record uses the word three times and the King James Bible seven. Verse 7 pairs it with repenting as what prevents the removal.
The purpose behind an act. The record uses the word thirty-two times and the King James Bible eleven. Verse 8 asks that the seeking be real.

phrases.term: Elders, priests, and teachers were baptized
phrases.text: The officers named first among the baptized. Moroni 3 had just described ordaining two of these.

phrases.term: Save they brought forth fruit meet that they were worthy of it
phrases.text: The first condition. Something had to be visible before the water.

phrases.term: They came forth with a broken heart and a contrite spirit
phrases.text: The second condition, given in the language of the offering. It describes what they brought, not what they said.

phrases.term: Witnessed unto the church that they truly repented of all their sins
phrases.text: The third condition. The witness is made to the congregation.

phrases.term: Having a determination to serve him to the end
phrases.text: The fourth condition, and the only one about the future. It is a resolve rather than a record.

phrases.term: Their names were taken, that they might be remembered and nourished
phrases.text: Why a list was kept. The record exists so people are not lost track of.

phrases.term: Relying alone upon the merits of Christ
phrases.text: Where the church was to lean. The word alone rules out the alternatives.

phrases.term: The author and the finisher of their faith
phrases.text: The title given him at the end of the verse. Hebrews 12:2 uses the same pair.

phrases.term: To speak one with another concerning the welfare of their souls
phrases.text: What the meetings were for. The talking is mutual and the subject is named.

phrases.term: Three witnesses of the church did condemn them before the elders
phrases.text: The procedure for discipline. It takes a number and a venue.

phrases.term: As oft as they repented and sought forgiveness, with real intent, they were forgiven
phrases.text: The clause that reverses verse 7. There is no limit set on how often.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: Officers baptized after they are officers
verses.text: The chapter's first substantive sentence puts the order in a way a reader may not expect: "elders, priests, and teachers were baptized; and they were not baptized save they brought forth fruit meet that they were worthy of it." Three offices are named and all three are said to have been baptized, which means ordination is not treated here as sufficient. The clause about fruit sets a condition on the rite for the people already holding the offices that would administer it.

verses.label: v. 4
verses.title: A membership roll, and what it was for
verses.text: The record describes an administrative act and gives its purpose: "their names were taken, that they might be remembered and nourished by the good word of God, to keep them in the right way." Two reasons are attached to the list, memory and nourishment, and both are about the church's obligation to the person rather than the person's standing in the church. Nothing about the roll is described as a check on anyone.

verses.label: v. 5–6
verses.title: Two kinds of meeting, distinguished and both frequent
verses.text: The record separates them and uses the same adverb for each: they "did meet together oft, to fast and to pray, and to speak one with another concerning the welfare of their souls," and they "did meet together oft to partake of bread and wine, in remembrance of the Lord Jesus." One gathering is for fasting, prayer and conversation, the other for a meal. Oft is the only measure of frequency the chapter gives, and it gives it twice.

verses.label: v. 7–8
verses.title: Discipline with a procedure, and forgiveness with none
verses.text: The record makes the expulsion clause specific about evidence: "whoso was found to commit iniquity, and three witnesses of the church did condemn him before the elders." A number of witnesses, a body to hear them, and an outcome, "his name was blotted out." Verse 8 states the reverse with no procedure at all: "as oft as they repented and sought forgiveness, with real intent, they were forgiven." The record specifies the machinery for putting someone out and none for taking them back.

verses.label: v. 9
verses.title: A church order that specifies no order
verses.text: The record describes how meetings ran, and the description is a refusal to prescribe: "their meetings were conducted by the church after the manner of the workings of the Spirit, and by the power of the Holy Ghost; for as the power of the Holy Ghost led them whether to preach, or to exhort, or to pray, or to supplicate, or to sing, even so it was done." Five activities are listed and no sequence is given for them. A chapter that has just set out conditions, records and disciplinary procedure ends by leaving the service itself unscripted.

chapter.title: The officers go through the same door
chapter.text: Verse 1 puts elders, priests, and teachers in the list of the baptized.

chapter.title: Four conditions are given before any water
chapter.text: Verses 1 through 3 ask for fruit, a broken heart, a public witness, and a determination.

chapter.title: Only the last condition looks forward
chapter.text: Verse 3 asks for a resolve to serve to the end, where the first three report on what has happened.

chapter.title: Names were written down for the sake of care
chapter.text: Verse 4 gives the list a purpose: remembering, nourishing, and keeping people watchful.

chapter.title: The church met for two different things
chapter.text: Verse 5 gives fasting, prayer, and talk; verse 6 gives bread and wine.

chapter.title: Discipline is spelled out and then reversed
chapter.text: Verse 7 removes a name and verse 8 restores anyone who repents with real intent.

chapter.title: No limit is put on forgiveness
chapter.text: Verse 8 says as oft as they repented.

chapter.title: The order of a meeting was left open
chapter.text: Verse 9 names five things and lets the Spirit choose among them.

applications.title: Ask for evidence before admission
applications.text: None were baptized save they brought forth fruit meet, came with a broken heart and a contrite spirit, and witnessed to the church that they truly repented. Three separate things are required, and a statement of belief is not one of them.

applications.title: Say what you intend to do afterward
applications.text: None were received save they took upon them the name of Christ with a determination to serve him to the end. Entry is described as the beginning of a commitment rather than the reward for one.

applications.title: Keep a list so people are looked after
applications.text: The names were taken so that no one would go unremembered or unfed.

applications.title: Meet often enough to know each other
applications.text: They spoke together about the welfare of their souls, which takes more than a greeting.

applications.title: Meet often for the same small thing
applications.text: They met together oft to partake of bread and wine in remembrance of the Lord Jesus. Repetition is the mechanism here, and the verse makes no apology for how ordinary it is.

applications.title: Three witnesses before a name comes off
applications.text: Discipline required three witnesses of the church to condemn before the elders, and it proceeded only if the person repented not and confessed not. A community strict about conduct still built two exits into the procedure.

applications.title: Make the way back short
applications.text: Repentance with real intent restored anyone, however often.

applications.title: Let the Spirit set the agenda
applications.text: Five possible things, and the choice was made in the moment.

questions.text: What fruit would show that I am ready for what I am asking for?
When did I last come to God with a broken heart?
Have I settled on serving to the end, or only for now?
Who am I meant to be nourishing by the good word of God?
Whom do I speak with about the welfare of my soul?
Is there iniquity I am being strict about, or quietly tolerating?
What am I seeking forgiveness for without real intent?
